extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent examiners (Korea), and practitioners advising on Korean domestic priority and patent-term-extension rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examination guidance on making, amending, examining, and applying the effects of a domestic priority claim under the Korean Patent Act, and criteria/procedures for applying for patent-term extension for regulatory approvals. Targets applicants and KIPO examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority claim based on a patent application ('Domestic Priority claim') is designed to ensure protection for inventions developed based on a prior-filed patent application to further specify, improve or add to the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invention identical to that disclosed in the prior-filed application is deemed filed on the prior-filed application's filing date; an invention newly added is deemed filed on the later-filed application's filing date. This addresses rejections that arose when improvements were filed as ordinary separate applications or added to prior-filed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a domestic priority claim (identity of applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who can make a domestic priority claim is the applicant of the prior-filed application (including a successor in title under Article 38(4)). The applicants of both the prior-filed and later-filed applications shall be identical at the time of filing the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For jointly filed applications applicants of the later-filed must match those of the prior-filed; to prove identicalness, residential/business address, name/title, and seals of applicants should be identical. If applicant names differ and succession is not proven, the examiner shall invalidate the domestic priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time requirement for domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed application shall be filed within one year from the filing date of the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This one-year period is measured from the filing date of the prior-filed application. Multiple prior-filed applications use their respective filing dates when calculating later effects (e.g., withdrawal deemed dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive basis for domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A domestic priority claim can be made based on the invention disclosed in the specification or drawings originally attached to the prior-filed application; inventions disclosed outside the claims can serve as the basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not required that the invention be present in the claims of the prior-filed application; any invention disclosed in the original spec/drawings qualifies as basis matter for retroactive filing date for that invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application ineligible if divisional or converted
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application must be neither a divisional application nor a converted application to serve as the basis of a domestic priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a divisional or converted application cannot be the basis of the domestic priority claim, a divisional or converted application can be filed later based on the application that claims domestic priority. The prohibition aims to reduce complexity in examination and date calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application must be pending / not invalidated at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application shall not be invalidated, withdrawn or abandoned, nor shall a decision to grant a patent or utility model registration have become final and binding at the time of filing the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to grant becomes final when a certified copy of the decision is delivered to the applicant; a decision to reject becomes final when 30 days have elapsed since the applicant received a certified copy. If the prior-filed application was withdrawn/abandoned on the filing date of the later-filed application, the priority claim may nonetheless be deemed valid provided it was made earlier than the invalidation time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure: statement of purport and prior-filed application at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A person making a domestic priority shall state the purport and identify the prior-filed application in the written patent application at the time of filing the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of evidential documents for priority is not necessary at filing; validity is determined based on the cover sheet of the prior-filed application. Where Article 30 exceptions are used, evidential documents under Article 30(2) must be submitted within the statutory period unless identical documents were already submitted for the prior-filed application (in which case the applicant may indicate those evidential documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on disclosure-exception claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim of disclosure exception was not made at the time of filing a prior-filed application, such a claim is not allowed when filing an application claiming priority to that prior-filed application (applies to applications filed on or before 28 July 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat domestic priority differently from Treaty priority regarding retroactivity under Article 30: Treaty priority cannot take the retroactive filing date under Article 30 whereas domestic priority can retain that retroactive filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority claim when filing divisional/converted application
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a divisional application or converted application based on an application claiming a domestic priority, the domestic priority claim shall be made at the time of filing the divisional or converted application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the domestic priority claim concurrently with filing the divisional/converted application to retain the priority linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of domestic priority on retroactive filing date (scope of retroactivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an invention identical with the one disclosed in the specification or drawings of the prior-filed application that forms the basis of the priority claim, the later-filed application is deemed to have been filed at the time of filing the prior-filed application for specified statutory provisions (e.g., novelty, inventive step, exceptions to public disclosure, first-to-file rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance lists specific Patent Act provisions for which the retroactive date applies: Article 29(1),(2) (novelty, inventive step), main sentence of Article 29(3) (enlarged concept of novelty), Article 30(1) (exception to public disclosure), Article 36(1)-(3) (first-to-file), Article 96(1)(3), Article 98, Article 103, Article 105(1),(2), Article 129, Article 136(5) (trial for a correction). Exclude inventions not disclosed in the prior-filed spec/drawings; those are examined from the later filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on double recognition of priority (avoiding extension of priority period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a prior-filed application already contains a domestic or Treaty priority claim, recognizing the priority claim twice in a later-filed application would technically extend the priority period; therefore the priority claim to inventions disclosed in the basis application shall not be acknowledged twice — effects apply only to inventions newly added to the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain retroactive effect on inventions disclosed in the basis application of the prior-filed application, multiple priority claims must be made based on that basis application in the later-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed withdrawal timing of prior-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application which forms the basis of a domestic priority claim is deemed to have been withdrawn when one year and three months have elapsed from the filing date of the prior-filed application, subject to exceptions (e.g., prior-filed has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or decision to grant has become final and binding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior-filed application has been invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned at the time in question, it is not deemed withdrawn. For multiple prior-filed applications, each is deemed withdrawn separately one year and three months after its own filing date. Note: pending applications are laid open; deemed-withdrawn prior-filed applications are not laid open unless early publication was requested within the 1y3m period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal restrictions for later-filed application and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed application claiming domestic priority can be withdrawn anytime, but after one year and three months have elapsed from the filing date of the prior-filed application, the domestic priority claim cannot be withdrawn. If the later-filed application is withdrawn within one year and three months of the prior-filed filing date, the domestic priority claim is deemed withdrawn simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later-filed application is withdrawn within 1y3m and the priority claim is simultaneously withdrawn, the prior-filed application will not be deemed withdrawn even though 1y3m has elapsed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right and timing to amend or add domestic priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend or add a domestic priority claim within one year and four months from the filing date of the prior-filed application (earliest filing date if multiple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The person allowed to amend/add is the applicant who met Article 55(1) requirements and made the priority claim at the time of filing. At least one domestic priority claim at filing must have satisfied Article 55(1) to permit later amendment/addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for an application to be added to domestic priority claim (Article 55(1) conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that can be added must meet these requirements: (i) prior-filed app filed within one year prior to the later-filed filing date; (ii) prior-filed app is not a divisional or converted application; (iii) prior-filed app has not been invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned and a decision to grant is not final; (iv) applicant of prior-filed is identical to applicant of later-filed; (v) items related to the priority claim are written clearly enough to specify the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing for determination: requirement (i) is assessed at the time of filing the later-filed application; requirements (iii) and (iv) are assessed at the time of amending or adding the priority claim. The law treats claims based on theoretical, another person's, or unspecified applications as inherently invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible amendments to domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year and four months from the filing date of the prior-filed application the applicant may wholly or partially withdraw priority claims in multiple priority claims, correct clerical errors, or add priority claims; after that period, amendments are limited to clerical errors only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority claims cannot be withdrawn once 1y3m have elapsed since the prior-filed filing date. For multiple priority claims, whether 1y3m elapsed is determined from the earliest filing dates of each relevant prior-filed application. To change a withdrawn priority and add another, an amendment copy with all amended features suffices — no separate written withdrawal notice is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination of domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing an application claiming domestic priority or an amendment, the examiner shall examine the formalities of the priority claim based on the specification and written amendment; if errors are found, the examiner requests amendment and may invalidate the domestic priority procedure if irregularities persist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subject of formality examination covers the whole requirements of the domestic priority claim except unity of invention. The allowable scope of amendment can vary depending on whether 1y4m has elapsed from the prior-filed filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality exam for international applications entering national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: When an international patent application claiming priority based on a domestic application or an international application designating only Korea enters the national phase, the examiner must determine whether the prior-filed application is pending at the time of formality examination since such priority claim is deemed domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior-filed application has been invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned or a decision to grant has become final and binding at the filing date of the international application, the examiner shall request the applicant to amend; failure to correct leads to invalidation of the priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination when domestic priority claim invalidated
rubrics_metrics.description: If the domestic priority claim is invalidated due to irregularities, the examiner shall examine the application based on its actual (later-filed) filing date rather than applying retroactive dates to determine patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a domestic priority claim is invalidated, the prior-filed application is not deemed to have been withdrawn; examiners must be careful in applying Article 36 (first-to-file) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination applying retroactive dates by invention
rubrics_metrics.description: When the domestic priority claim is valid, the examiner shall consider retroactive date calculations by invention: inventions disclosed in the prior-filed application's original specification/drawings are examined as if filed on the prior-filed date; inventions not disclosed are examined from the filing date of the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This parallels Treaty priority practice: retroactivity is applied on an invention-by-invention basis, not wholesale for the entire application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner instruction regarding deferred examination of prior-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the prior-filed application forming the basis of a domestic priority claim is deemed withdrawn when 1 year and three months have elapsed, the examiner shall not start examination of the prior-filed application but defer it; the same applies to requests for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should perform formality examination of the priority claim promptly after filing the later-filed application to avoid unfairly causing the prior-filed application to be deemed withdrawn or depriving applicant of refiling opportunities. Examiners may request amendments in the name of the KIPO commissioner for items omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of invalid domestic priority claim for examination status
rubrics_metrics.description: If the domestic priority claim violates Article 55(1) or is invalidated (e.g., applicants are not identical), the priority claim is deemed never made and has no legal effects; the examiner shall change the status (e.g., cancel deferral/withdrawal) and resume examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases the prior-filed application may become another application under Article 29(3) or a prior-filed application under Article 36; the later-filed application shall be treated as a regular application without any priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term extension eligibility (Article 89 general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patented invention prescribed by Presidential Decree requires approval or registration under other statutes to be practiced and it takes a long time to undergo necessary tests (efficacy, safety, etc.), the patent term may be extended only once by up to five years to compensate for the period during which the invention cannot be practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Period attributable to the person who received the approval (applicant) is excluded from the 'period during which the invention cannot be practiced' when calculating extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions prescribed by Enforcement Decree Article 7 (eligible classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Invention prescribed by Presidential Decree' includes: (1) medicines which received approval under certain provisions of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act (limited to medicines with a new active substance and limited to first approvals among those with new substances); (2) agricultural chemicals or raw materials registered under specified provisions of the Pesticide Control Act (limited to first registrations among those with new substances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is narrowly defined to first approvals/registrations of inventions involving a 'new substance' active moiety; other inventions are not eligible even if approval caused delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patents eligible for term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A patented invention entitled to registration for an extension of the patent term may be a product patent, process patent, use patent, or composition patent as defined by Article 89 and Article 7(1) of the Enforcement Decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an invention corresponds to Article 7(1) of the Enforcement Decree, whether it took long to obtain approval or registration is not considered for determining whether it is an 'invention prescribed by Presidential Decree'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable law on approval/registration for term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable statutes for approvals/registrations that qualify include the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act for medicines and the Pesticide Control Act for agricultural chemicals/raw materials; only inventions that required such approvals/registrations and were not practiced for a period due to obtaining the approvals are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions which required approvals under other Acts but are not of the specific kinds listed (e.g., not medicines/new agricultural chemicals) are excluded even if practice was delayed for approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and validity conditions for filing extension application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of an extension of the patent term can be filed only while the patent right is still valid. If the patent right has been invalidated, cancelled, or extinguished (e.g., for failure to pay fees), the extension application is not valid. If a trial to invalidate is pending, the application may still be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent was valid at the time of filing the extension application but becomes invalid thereafter, the examiner shall give the applicant an opportunity to explain under procedural rules; failing adequate explanation, the extension application will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination rules when multiple approvals / ingredients / patents involved
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) If multiple approvals are obtained for multiple active ingredients disclosed in a single patent, the applicant may choose one permitted ingredient and apply for a one-time extension for that ingredient. (ii) If multiple approvals relate to the same active ingredient disclosed in a single patent, only the initial approval is eligible for the extension application. (iii) If a single approval implicates multiple patents (e.g., product, process, use patents), the term of each patented invention relevant to that approval may be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (i) For active ingredients A, B, C with separate approvals, choose one ingredient for the one-time extension. (ii) For sequential approvals for the same ingredient (product approval A then API B then dosage-form change C), only the initial approval A can be the basis. (iii) Where multiple patents cover the same approved product, separate extension applications can be filed for each patent in relation to the same approval (subject to other statutory limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of applicant-attributable delay from extension period
rubrics_metrics.description: Any portion of the approval/registration period attributable to the person who received the approval (e.g., applicant-caused delays) shall not be included in the period counted as 'period during which the invention cannot be practiced' for purposes of patent-term extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing eligible extension length, deduct delays caused by the patentee/applicant's actions; only legitimately unavoidable regulatory delay counts toward the extension.
